words.gloss: concerning knowledge of abnormal limbs/body parts

hindi: अब इसलिए हम विकृत अंगों के ज्ञान वाले अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on the knowledge of abnormal body parts (vikṛtāṅgavijñānīya).
notes: Standard chapter-opening formula. The chapter title is read as vikṛta-aṅga-vijñānīya, 'concerning the knowledge of abnormal limbs/parts of the body'; the adjective qualifies adhyāyam.

hindi: स्वस्थ या रोगी पुरुषों में, जो दूसरे शरीर की इच्छा करने वाले हैं, औषध की पहुँच से परे गए, पूरे शरीर में फैलने वाले दोष, बादल जैसे वर्षा को सूचित करते हैं वैसे ही आयु के क्षय को सूचित करते हुए, अचानक स्वभाव का विपर्यास उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: The doṣas (humours) that have gone beyond the range of medicine and pervade the whole body, in men, whether healthy or afflicted, who desire another body, indicating the decay of life as clouds (indicate) rain, suddenly produce a reversal of natural state.

text_flags.why: possible: 'svasthanām' lacks the long ā of the genitive plural svasthānām; the split svastha-nām is also conceivable but gives no sense

notes: Elliptical comparison: 'ghanāghanā iva varṣam' takes its participle sūcayantaḥ from the next phrase (clouds indicating rain). ghanāghana is read as 'cloud'; other senses (dense, elephant) are not suitable here. The genitive plurals (of the healthy or afflicted men) are rendered 'in men'. dehāntarābhilāṣiṇām is literally 'desiring another body'; the text does not say 'dying'. Normalisation: viparyyāsa (doubled y) read viparyāsa.

hindi: उसे संक्षेप में रिष्ट यानी अनिष्ट सूचक लक्षण कहते हैं।
english: In brief, they call that riṣṭa (an ill-omen, a sign of approaching death).
notes: riṣṭa is a doctrinal term (a sign foretelling death); the gloss is a plain explanation, not a modern equivalent.

words.gloss: colours of the body's natural state

hindi: उनमें गौर या अगौर, श्याम या अश्याम, कृष्ण या अकृष्ण, ये देह की प्रकृति के वर्ण हैं।
english: Among these: fair or not fair, dusky or not dusky, black or not black: these are the colours of the body's natural state.

text_flags.why: possible: a+i has been joined into ai; akṛṣṇaḥ + iti should give akṛṣṇa iti (the same printing habit as in the neighbouring pairs)

notes: The meaning of the a- forms is literal 'not fair' etc.; a sense 'slightly' (not very fair) is possible but not stated. 'or' is supplied to show the pairs; the text has none. prakṛti here is rendered 'natural state'.

words.gloss: lotus-fair and the like (padma = lotus, Nelumbo nucifera; standard)

hindi: और उनके भेद पद्मगौर यानी कमल के समान गौर आदि हैं।
english: And its varieties are lotus-fair (padmagaura) and the like.
notes: Verb understood (copula); none supplied beyond 'are'. padmagaura is read as 'fair like a lotus'; padma = lotus, Nelumbo nucifera (standard).

words.gloss: blue, dusky, copper-coloured, turmeric-yellow (haridrā, Curcuma longa; standard), white and the like
the natural-state colour and the abnormal colour

hindi: नील, श्याम, ताम्र, हारिद्र यानी हल्दी के रंग के, शुक्ल आदि तो विकृतियाँ हैं। उनमें प्रकृति का वर्ण और विकृति का वर्ण, एक साथ, या अनुमानित पाठ पर शरीर के एक भाग में, मृत्यु के लिए होते हैं।
english: But blue, dusky, copper-coloured, turmeric-yellow, white and the like are abnormalities. Among these, the natural-state colour and the abnormal colour together at once, or on a conjectural reading in one part of the body, are for death.

text_flags.why: possible: 'gaṃdhega' is meaningless here; 'gātra-ekadeśe' (in one part of the body) fits the sense and the printed letters loosely (gā-tra / gaṃdhe-ga)
possible: extra t in 'śyāmat-tāmra'; read śyāma-tāmra

notes: The word 'yugapadgaṃdhegaikadeśe' is damaged and kept unsplit; the conjecture 'yugapad gātra-ekadeśe' (at once, or in one part of the body) is used in the translations and marked as conjectural. 'vikṛtayaḥtatra' has a missing space (vikṛtayaḥ tatra). The verb is understood ('are'). maraṇāya is dative, 'for death', i.e. leading to death.

words.gloss: fading, growth, grief, joy, dryness, unctuousness and the like
of those stated in the (passage) on varieties of prakṛti
by the division of doṣas etc.

hindi: इससे मुरझाना, वृद्धि, शोक, हर्ष, रूखापन, स्निग्धता आदि, तथा प्रकृतिभेदीय में कहे गए बड़े, उपचित, सूक्ष्म, दीर्घ, और दोष आदि के भाग से नियत सभी भावों का बिना कारण अन्यथा होना कहा गया है।
english: By this, the being otherwise without cause of fading, growth, grief, joy, dryness, unctuousness and the like, and likewise of all the states stated in the (passage) on varieties of prakṛti (large, plump, fine, long) and determined by the division of doṣas etc., is stated.

text_flags.why: possible: 'uracaya' is not a word; 'upacaya' (growth), the same word as in mahadupacaya later in the line, fits the sense (r misread for p); also the missing space after etena

notes: The construction is loose; the genitives 'prakṛtibhedīyoktānām ... sarveṣām ... bhāvānām' are taken as the things whose being otherwise is stated, and the list in the nominative is taken with the same. mlāni = fading, withering; upacaya = growth, plumpness (alternatives possible). 'prakṛtibhedīya' is read as the section on the varieties of prakṛti; its identity is not stated in the line. 'pratiniyatānāṃbhāvānām' has a missing space.

hindi: शरीर में छायाएँ पाँच हैं।
english: As for the chāyās (shades or lustres), there are five in the body.
notes: chāyā is a technical term: shade, lustre or reflection of the body; the next units describe the five by element, so it is kept as chāyā with the general gloss 'shade, lustre'.

hindi: उनमें अनुमानित पाठ पर आकाश से, निर्मल, तलवार और आकाश के समान नीली, स्वच्छ, स्निग्ध, मानो प्रभा सहित।
english: Among these, on a conjectural reading, the one from ether (kha), stainless, blue like a sword and the sky, clear, unctuous, as if with lustre (prabhā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'khādamla' is not intelligible; the pattern of units 10 to 13 (vātāt, tejasaḥ, aṃbhasaḥ, bhuvaḥ) calls for an ablative of the element (khāt, from ether) and amala 'stainless' fits; 'khaṅga' probably for 'khaḍga' (sword), ḍ/ṅ confusion

notes: The long compound is damaged and kept unsplit; the reading in the translations is a conjecture. The element is ether (ākāśa), by the pattern of the next four units. 'saprabheva' = saprabhā iva.

hindi: वायु से आने वाली छाया धूल और राख के समान रूखी, धूल से लाल, श्याव, प्रभाहीन और स्वेदमल की गन्ध वाली होती है।
english: From vāyu (wind): dry as dust and ash, dust-reddish, dark brown, lacking lustre, smelling of sweat-waste (sveda-mala).
notes: The noun chāyā is understood from unit 8 (the five shades); no noun is stated here, the adjectives are feminine singular. 'pāṃśubhasmarūkṣā' is read 'dry as dust and ash'; 'rajo'ruṇā' 'reddish with dust' (rajas read as dust; no other sense is stated). The final 'gandhiḥ' is a masculine-type ending used with feminine agreement; read as printed. mala here is the waste (sveda-mala, sweat-waste), not an added disease.

hindi: तेजस् यानी अग्नि से आने वाली छाया, अनुमानित पाठ पर हवन की अग्नि, बिजली और सोने के समान लाल, दृष्टि और मुख वाली होती है।
english: From tejas (fire): on a conjectural reading, red like an oblation-fed fire, lightning and gold; dṛṣṭimukhā (with eye and face).

text_flags.why: possible: the letters 'asa' after vidyut are unaccounted for; the compound is read as 'red like sacrificed-to fire, lightning and gold (tapanīya)'

notes: The compound is damaged and kept unsplit; the reading in the translations is a conjecture (huta-hutāśa = fire fed with oblation, tapanīya = gold). 'dṛṣṭimukhā' is rendered literally 'with eye and face'; the text does not say that the colour shows in the eyes and face, though this is probable. Normalisation: tejas read as the element fire.

words.gloss: clear as vaidūrya (beryl or cat's-eye; identity disputed) and indranīla (sapphire; probable)

hindi: जल से आने वाली छाया वैदूर्य यानी लहसुनिया, पर पहचान विवादित है, और अनुमानित पाठ पर इन्द्रनील यानी सम्भवतः नीलम के समान निर्मल, घनी और अत्यन्त स्निग्ध होती है।
english: From water (ambhas): clear as vaidūrya (beryl or cat's-eye; identity disputed) and, on a conjectural reading, indranīla (probably sapphire); dense, very unctuous.

text_flags.why: possible: 'indrīla' is not a word; 'indranīla' (sapphire) fits the pattern of gem comparisons and the letters

notes: Noun chāyā understood from unit 8. vaidūrya: disputed (cat's-eye chrysoberyl or beryl); indranīla: probably sapphire (a blue gem).

hindi: पृथ्वी से आने वाली छाया सुन्दर कान्ति वाली, घनी, स्थिर, स्निग्ध, अनुमानित पाठ पर शुद्ध, श्याम और श्वेत होती है।
english: From earth: of pleasing lustre, dense, steady, unctuous, on a conjectural reading pure, dusky and white.

text_flags.why: possible: as printed the regular sandhi reading is snigdhā + aśuddhā 'unctuous, impure', which sits oddly in a list of good qualities; 'snigdhā śuddhā' (missing space) is assumed

notes: Noun chāyā understood from unit 8. Alternative: aśuddhā 'impure' as the print stands.

hindi: उनमें वायु वाली छाया विनाश के लिए और अत्यन्त बड़े क्लेश के लिए होती है; शेष तो सुख के उदय वाली हैं।
english: Of these, the one of vāyu (wind) is for destruction and for very great affliction; the remaining ones are, however, bringers of a rise of happiness.
notes: 'atimahate' is taken with kleśāya (for very great affliction); the noun is not repeated in the text. sukhodaya is literally 'rise of happiness'.

hindi: प्रभाएँ सात हैं: रक्त यानी लाल, पीली, पाण्डुर यानी फीकी, सित यानी सफेद, असित यानी काली, श्याव यानी गहरी भूरी और हरी।
english: There are seven prabhās (radiances): red, yellow, pale, white, black, dark brown and green.

text_flags.why: possible: visarga before c should become ś (haritāś ca); printed without it

notes: Final -āḥ before a voiced consonant is regular sandhi in raktā, pītā etc. asita is rendered 'black' (literally 'not white'); harita 'green' (it can also mean yellowish-green). The 'sitā 'sitā' pair is sitāḥ asitāḥ.

hindi: वे स्निग्ध, विकसित होने वाली और निर्मल प्रभाएँ शुभ हैं; विपरीत तो अशुभ हैं।
english: Those (that are) unctuous, spreading and stainless are auspicious; the opposite (ones) are inauspicious.
notes: 'tāḥ' refers to the prabhās of unit 15. vikāśin is rendered 'spreading, radiant' (blooming, expanding).

hindi: उन दोनों का भेद।
english: The distinction between the two.
notes: Elliptical; the two are not named in the unit. By position they are chāyā and prabhā (units 18 and 19), but this is not stated. No verb supplied.

hindi: छाया वर्ण पर छा जाती है, समीप है, अनुमानित पाठ पर और दिखाई देती है, और पाँच भूतों से बनी है।
english: The chāyā overspreads the colour; it is near; on a conjectural reading it is also perceived; and it consists of the five elements (bhūta).

text_flags.why: possible: 'calacyate' is not a word; the contrast with unit 19 (prabhā ... viprakṛṣṭā lakṣyate) suggests 'ca lakṣyate' (kṣ read as c)

notes: Damaged word: 'calacyate' read as 'ca lakṣyate' on the model of unit 19; the translation marks this. ākrāmati: 'overspreads, covers'.

hindi: प्रभा तो वर्ण को प्रकाशित करती है, दूर से दिखाई देती है, और तेजस् की प्रभा ही है।
english: The prabhā, however, illuminates the colour; it is perceived from afar; and it is just the radiance of tejas (fire).
notes: 'tejaḥprabhaiva' could also be read tejaḥ, prabhā eva ('tejas, itself prabhā'); the compound reading is used. Missing spaces in the long token.

words.gloss: kumārikā (little girl: probably the figure seen in the pupil)

hindi: जिसकी दृष्टि में प्रतिबिम्ब से बनी कुमारिका यानी सम्भवतः पुतली में दिखने वाली छोटी कन्या नहीं दिखाई देती, वह परासु यानी जिसके प्राण चले गए हैं।
english: He in whose eye the little girl (kumārikā, probably the small figure seen in the pupil) made of reflection is not seen is parāsu (one whose life-breath has gone).
notes: kumārikā literally 'little girl'; probable sense: the small reflected figure in the pupil (probable). dṛṣṭi is taken as 'eye' (sight). 'parāsu' literally 'whose breaths (asu) have gone away'; the verb 'is' is understood.

words.gloss: in sunlight, mirror and the like

hindi: जिसकी, अनुमानित पाठ पर धूप और दर्पण आदि में, अचानक प्रतिच्छाया कटी हुई, फटी हुई, हीन, अधिक, व्याकुल, नष्ट, अनुमानित पाठ पर टेढ़ी, नीचे सिर वाली, सिरहीन, दो सिर वाली, फैली हुई, अन्य प्रकार की या विकृत दिखाई देती है।
english: He whose reflection (praticchāyā), in sunlight, on a conjectural reading mirror, and the like, is suddenly seen cut, split, deficient, in excess, confused, lost, on a conjectural reading crooked, with head downward, headless, two-headed, spread out, otherwise, or distorted.

text_flags.why: possible: ātapa + ādarśa (mirror) gives ātapādarśa; the printed form lacks one ā; 'darśa' alone does not suit the list
possible: 'jihyā' is not a word; jihmā (crooked) with h/m and y/m confusion, and a close pattern in unit 28

notes: No predicate follows in this unit (the clause continues in the same series of conditions); the main clause is not given here. Two conjectural readings (ādarśa, jihmā) are marked in the translations. The word 'adhikā' next to 'hīnā' read as deficient / in excess.

hindi: जिसका ललाट पसीजता नहीं।
english: He whose forehead does not sweat.
notes: Relative clause only; the main clause is not in this unit.

hindi: जिसके केश और रोम बिना तेल लगे होने पर तेल लगे हुए के समान दिखाई देते हैं।
english: He whose head-hair and body-hair, unanointed, are seen as if anointed.
notes: One token with a missing space after yasya. abhyakta = anointed with oil or ointment.

words.gloss: of the colour of a firebrand
of abnormal colour such as blue

hindi: और दोनों आँखें बहुत भीतर धँसी हुई, बाहर निकली हुई, फैली हुई, सिकुड़ी हुई; सिकुड़ी भौंहों वाली, झुकी भौंहों वाली; अनुमानित पाठ पर टेढ़ी, ऊँची-नीची; रुकी हुई दृष्टि वाली, क्षीण दृष्टि वाली; नकुल के समान, कपोत के समान, जलती लकड़ी के रंग की, नील आदि विकृत रंग की; बहुत चंचल, कड़ी और ढीली, बहती हुई, बहुत खुली, बहुत मिची हुई, या झड़ी पलकों वाली।
english: And the two eyes: sunk in too deep, protruding, widened, contracted; with contracted brows, with bent-down brows; on a conjectural reading crooked, uneven; with ceased sight, with deficient sight; resembling a mongoose (nakula), resembling a pigeon (kapota), of the colour of a firebrand, of abnormal colour such as blue; very unsteady, stiff and drooping, discharging, too widely open, too tightly shut, or with lost eyelashes.

text_flags.why: possible: 'jihve' would be dual 'two tongues'; the list is of eye qualities and the neuter dual 'jihme' (crooked) fits (compare unit 21, 28)
possible: the final member should be a dual of bhrū; 'bhruṇī' is irregular (compare pakṣmaṇī, a true -man dual); sense unaffected
possible: same irregular dual as the preceding word

notes: GROUPING: the unit has no 'yasya' and no main verb; it appears to continue the series of conditions of units 22 and 23 and to be completed in unit 25. All adjectives agree with nayane (two eyes). 'viśrānta' is kept as printed (ceased, rested); 'vibhrānta' (confused) is an alternative. nakula = mongoose (standard); the colour comparison is meant, not stated as such. 'stabdhasraste' is read as dvandva 'stiff and drooping'. Conjectural reading: jihme.

words.gloss: covered with piṭikās (small boils or pustules)

hindi: या नाक बहुत खुली, बहुत बन्द, टेढ़ी, फटी हुई, पिटिका यानी छोटी फुंसियों से ढकी या सूखी, वह गतायु यानी जिसकी आयु जा चुकी है।
english: Or the nose too wide open, too closed, crooked, cracked, covered with piṭikās (small boils or pustules) or dry: he is gatāyu (one whose life-span has gone).
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete the series of conditions begun in units 22 to 24 (the main clause 'sa gatāyuḥ' occurs only here). The leading avagraha on 'tivivṛtā is a print habit for vā + ati. piṭikā: small boil, pustule.

words.gloss: ripe jambū fruit (Syzygium cumini, Indian blackberry; standard)

hindi: जिसका निचला होंठ नीचे जाता है और ऊपरी होंठ, या दोनों ऊपर की ओर मुख वाले, या पके जामुन यानी जम्बू फल के समान नीले।
english: He whose lower lip goes downward, and upper lip, or the two (lips) facing upward, or blue like the ripe jambū fruit (Syzygium cumini, Indian blackberry).
notes: The construction is uncertain: 'yāti' may govern both lips (lower down, upper up) and 'ūrdhvamukhau' / 'nīlau' are dual adjectives of an unstated 'two lips'. The translation keeps the uncertainty and supplies no extra verb. jambū (jāmun) = Syzygium cumini (standard).

hindi: या दाँत बहुत रूखे, ताम्र, श्याम, कीचड़ वाले, पुष्पित, कंकड़ी के कणों वाले हैं, या अचानक गिर जाते हैं।
english: Or the teeth very dry, copper-coloured, dusky, muddy, flowered, with grit (śarkarā), or they suddenly fall out.
notes: puṣpita (literally 'flowered') is kept literal; the sense (a flower-like efflorescence) is not stated. śarkarā literally 'gravel, grit, sugar'; tartar is a possible sense (not stated). The first half has no verb ('are' understood); 'patanti' belongs to the last alternative.

hindi: या जीभ टेढ़ी, कड़ी, सुन्न, लिपी हुई, भारी, श्याव, सूजी हुई, सूखी, फैलने वाली, या मानो काँटों से ढकी हुई है।
english: Or the tongue crooked, stiff, numb, coated, heavy, dark brown, swollen, dry, spreading, or as if covered with thorns.

text_flags.why: possible: as printed stabdhā + asuptā would mean 'not numb'; the list of defects needs 'suptā' (missing space)

notes: 'visarpiṇī' is rendered 'spreading' only (it is not read as the disease visarpa). The 'iva vā' ending: kaṇṭaka-ācitā iva vā.

words.gloss: the attachments of cheek, forehead and jaw

hindi: जिसके गाल, ललाट और हनु के बन्धन मानो स्थान से च्युत और ढीले हैं, अनुमानित पाठ पर जिसका सिर, गर्दन या पीठ अपना भार नहीं सहता।
english: He whose attachments of cheek, forehead and jaw are slack as if fallen from their place; on a conjectural reading, whose head, neck or back does not bear its own weight.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dhante' is not a regular form; sense requires a verb 'holds, bears' (n/tt confusion)
possible: the neck as a subject (nominative) beside śiraḥ and pṛṣṭham; the final ṃ may be a print slip or may mark an accusative object

notes: The second half is uncertain. 'yasyana' = yasya na (space missing). The reading adopted (head, neck or back does not bear its own weight, svabhāram being the object) is a conjecture; the case endings in śirodharāṃ and svabhāraṃ may point to a different construction (he does not hold up ...). Unit 30 appears to continue the sentence.

hindi: या दोनों हनु, मुख में स्थित पिण्ड।
english: Or the two jaws, a lump staying in the mouth.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 29 (a verb such as 'do not hold' may be carried over, so 'the jaws ... the lump in the mouth'); no verb is supplied in the translation. Elliptical.

hindi: जिसका मेढ्र सूजा हुआ है, या दोनों वृषण बहुत बाहर निकले हैं, या इससे उलटा है।
english: He whose penis (meḍhra) is swollen, or whose two testicles (vṛṣaṇa) have gone out too far, or the reverse of this.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed 'atyi' has an extra y before iniḥ; 'ati-niḥsṛtau' (very much gone out) is intended

notes: 'niḥsṛta' (gone out) is kept literal: the text does not say whether the testicles are retracted or drawn down. utsikta: swollen, raised. 'ataḥ ... viparyayaḥ' = 'the reverse of this'.

hindi: जिसका मूत्र बहुत उग्र है।
english: He whose urine is very fierce (strong).
notes: Relative clause only; 'ugra' (fierce) is kept general and could refer to smell or sharpness, which the text does not say.

hindi: जिसके विष के दोष के बिना छिद्रों से रोमकूपों सहित रक्त बहता है।
english: He from whose orifices (kha), together with the hair-pores, blood flows out without the fault of poison.
notes: 'prabartate' is pravartate (v/b spelling, recorded normalisation). 'viṣadoṣāt vinā' is rendered literally; the text does not name the orifices.

words.gloss: one who wishes to die, about to die

hindi: जिसके अंग बिना कारण बहुत हल्के या बहुत भारी हों, वह मुमूर्षु यानी मरने की इच्छा वाला, मरने को उद्यत है।
english: He whose limbs would be, without cause, too light or too heavy: he is mumūrṣu (one about to die; literally 'wishing to die').
notes: mumūrṣu is a desiderative adjective, literally 'wishing to die'; 'about to die' is the usual sense.

hindi: जिसका स्वर एक या अनेक, या हकलाता हुआ, अव्यक्त, कृश या दीन अचानक सुनाई देता है।
english: He whose voice, single or manifold, or stammering, indistinct, thin or piteous, is suddenly perceived.

text_flags.why: possible: 'anyakta' is not a word; avyakta (indistinct) fits the list of voice defects (v read as n)

notes: 'ekaḥ anekaḥ' is kept literal (single or manifold). The corrected avyakta is adopted in the translations without a separate conjectural mark because the sense is certain from the list.

words.gram: desid. adj. vi+√vac, m. nom. sg.

hindi: या जो बोलना चाहता हुआ मोहित हो जाता है।
english: Or he who, wishing to speak, becomes bewildered.
notes: Relative clause; the main clause is not in this unit. muhyati: becomes bewildered, confused (it can also be 'faints'; the literal sense is kept).
